picked: GLM 5.3, filed at 753B parameters, FP8 (753 GB of weights, about 756 GB as published), GLM-5.3 bespoke licence, served on vLLM on one node in the plant's own server room in Pakistan
why: Bespoke licence permits commercial use, fine tuning and redistribution, so the operator names the model and fixes it to its own hardware; the agentic work surface and the ontology's maintainer: it drafts weld checks, traces supplier lots and answers questions conversationally with citations

picked: D-FINE, Apache-2.0 code and weights, COCO checkpoints, INT8 through ONNX Runtime on the 6 TOPS edge NPU; the N variant about 8 MB at 16 bit, the X variant about 124 MB
why: Apache-2.0 terms cover code and weights alike and the COCO checkpoints avoid the Objects365 terms that ship with other checkpoints; 42.8 to 55.8 COCO AP at 2.12 to 12.89 ms on a single T4 leaves wide margin at station pace; detects weld spots, parts, clips, connectors and fasteners at the station exits

picked: Anomalib 2.7.0, Apache-2.0 with edge export, FP32, on the edge units; footprint model dependent, typically tens to hundreds of MB, PatchCore memory banks grow with the reference set
why: Sealer gaps are rare and varied, so an unsupervised model fitted on the plant's own good beads beats any defect catalogue; the plant's own images replace the non commercial benchmark data the library ships with

picked: BGE-M3, MIT, FP16, about 1.1 GB (about 2.27 GB at FP32, about 0.6 GB at 8 bit), on the 48 GB site server
why: MIT licence with no obligation; dense, sparse and multi vector retrieval in one pass with an 8,192 token window, so part numbers and error codes stay retrievable and every conversational answer cites the record behind it

picked: 141 GB HBM GPU class, eight GPUs per node, one node (1,128 GB)
why: Holds GLM 5.3's 753 GB of FP8 weights on one node; the US export licence determination for this class runs at phase one start, with an approved data center or phased precision fallback kept on the table without quietly shrinking the model

picked: Frontier model GPU footprint sizing rule, vLLM
why: 753 GB of weights times the 1.2 planning factor is 904 GB against the node's 1,128 GB, leaving 375 GB beside the weights; at the roughly 756 GB the published weights occupy the KV cache ceiling is about 280 GB, which bounds concurrent sessions rather than forcing a second node

picked: GLM 5.3 node count by GPU class
why: One node of eight 141 GB GPUs; the plant server room GPU node ASHRAE class fixes the server room envelope

picked: Air cooled 48 GB PCIe inference class server, one, in the plant server room
why: Serves BGE-M3 at FP16 and re-scores the borderline detections the edge tier flags, a full precision second opinion without any frame leaving the plant; a US ECCN 3A090 licence determination for Pakistan is required before the class is quoted

picked: Fanless industrial edge unit on an octa core 6 TOPS NPU SoC, rated minus 40 to 85 C, sealed aluminium enclosure, pSLC storage, isolated 24 V trigger, wide input 24 V supply
why: Weld fume, spatter and summer heat exceed the ambient ratings of the packaged smart camera class; the unit runs the check on the device, buffers on disk through a lost link and keeps only the result and the evidence frame

picked: 5 MP global shutter GigE Vision cameras with strobed lighting at five station exits (body shop after spot welding and sealer, trim line stations, underbody), a body present trigger from the station PLC; controller, torque and end of line feeds
why: One capture per body freezes a moving body without rolling shutter skew; identity comes from the body number and MES genealogy, so no tracker is committed; cameras check bodies and vehicles, never worker performance

picked: OCP Time Card grandmaster with linuxptp (ptp4l, phc2sys)
why: Every event is stamped from the PTP grandmaster so a camera frame, a torque reading and a weld log sit on one timeline
Runs D-FINE and Anomalib at INT8 on the edge NPU units; K3s orchestrates the containers at the edge
Serves the FP8 weights of GLM 5.3 within the KV cache ceiling the sizing reserves

picked: Harbor, air gapped artifact and model registry, fed by a one way Lidi transfer; a data diode on any transfer out of a network zone
why: Model and container updates enter one way; an interrupted update leaves the running detector in place while the registry holds the last complete artifact

picked: Apache Kafka 4.4, TimescaleDB, Prometheus, Grafana and Loki
why: Ordering keyed by body number, at least once delivery with idempotent writes, on disk buffering at the edge; capture completeness is an alert the command centre sees

picked: Triggered one capture per body at each station exit
why: Adopted over multi object tracking because each body is captured once and identity is already owned by a system of record

picked: Nuisance images collected and labelled before any threshold is set
why: False alarms from ordinary plant grime are what switch inspection systems off; the false flag budget is held under 10 per inspector per shift and the nuisance set is a phase item with its own gate

picked: Memory over confirmed outcomes, nothing trained into weights
why: The requirement rules out training on the fly, and changing weights under audit would invalidate the validation evidence the parent's standards rest on

picked: The plant network in Pakistan, the operator's own hardware, no third party model service; read only adapters and the single approved write path to the quality management system
why: Images, process data and the parent's standards never leave the plant; the national data protection rules on cameras, the parent's audit terms and the localisation policy bind the design
